summary: Configured node1 with a persistent loopback backend on TCP 8091 and nginx reverse proxy on public TCP 8090. Both return `backend-ready`. Only 8090 is firewall-published. A full node restart changed the boot ID and all services, listeners, firewall rules, and responses recovered automatically.
actions_performed: Configured nginx to proxy TCP 8090 to 127.0.0.1:8091
Configured persistent SELinux and firewalld rules
Verified the proxy path through matching nginx and backend logs
Safely restarted node1 and verified persistence

evidence.requirement: Local backend on TCP 8091 returns backend-ready
evidence.summary: Shows backend-8091 enabled and active, listening on 127.0.0.1:8091, and returning HTTP 200 with `backend-ready`.
Shows nginx listening on 0.0.0.0/[::]:8090 and returning HTTP 200 with `backend-ready` through 10.100.70.10; matching request logs and proxy_pass configuration prove forwarding to port 8091.
Shows TCP 8090 allowed persistently and at runtime while backend TCP 8091 remains unpublished.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID e31962a9-8d32-4c19-8dd2-0b96a45c6c48, safe reboot acknowledgment, changed boot ID f42bbaf1-7b0e-45df-a8d2-379293612acc, and complete post-restart service/listener/HTTP/firewall recovery.
Shows both services active, correct listeners, direct and proxied HTTP 200 responses, and the same post-restart request recorded by nginx and the backend.
